w: A ‘Parents Day’ program was arranged in the evening assembly.

More than 450 devotees had participated in the maha-puja ceremony of the foundation stone laying ceremony for the new mandir in Detroit. More than 2,5000 people had gathered for the assembly that followed.
In the evening assembly the Kenton City Supervisor, Mr. Tom Yack, read and presented a proclamation to Swamishri.
Lord Harikrishna Maharaj was honored by the devotees.
Swamishri inaugurated and performed the murti-pratishtha at the Swaminarayan Sanskardham in Ambavadi - a suburb of Amdavad.
After his morning puja, Swamishri performed the pujan rituals of bricks for the Hari mandirs in the towns of Rapar, Morzar, Panandhro, Bhirandiyara and Ramnagar.
In the evening assembly Shri Harikrishna Maharaj (Thakorji) was honored by the devotees.
A school Day and Parents Day was held to celebrate the 35th anniversary of the Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan High School in Gondal. The Women's Wing also celebrated it as Bhakti Day.

The special morning assembly commenced with a traditional dance by balaks. The Principal, Shri Krishna Pandya, narrated the brief history of the school and its progress and results. Then the school students enacted a story from Yogiji Maharaj's parables. After honoring Swamishri with a shawl and garlands, Swamishri blessed the assembly, stressing the importance of moral and spiritual character in today's educational curriculum.
No matter how many speeches one delivers, if one has not imbibed it in life then one leaves no impact. (6-10-2003, Gondal).
Swamishri arrived in Nairobi by plane at 11.00 am.

Guest Speakers : Dr R Chidambaram, scientist and chief scientific adviser of India, said, “It is impossible to believe that all this has been achieved in a brief span of five years. You have mixed spirituality with high technology. What you are doing here in Akshardham in Delhi, and what of course you have done in London and in Gandhinagar, and in many other places, is to restore to India its great spiritual heritage.
Guests : Shri Bharatbhai Shah, industrialist and social worker, Dubai, reflected, “Only a Yugpurush (epoch-maker) sent by God can accomplish such a wonderful complex.”

Shri L.D. Mittal, owner of Sonalik Tractors, opined, “After seeing Akshardham I felt as if a magician has created this complex. In four to five years such a big structure! To make a small bungalow it takes four years. This is possible only through God’s grace. It is an amazing confluence of sculpture, science and bhakti.”

The Akshardham festival included a 25 day program of stage performances, speeches and blessings. Every morning Swamishri performed his morning puja on the festival stage. Thereafter he would return to his living quarters by car, during which thousands of devotees stood on both sides of the road to have Swamishri’s darshan. Today, while Swamishri was proceeding by car he saw an old devotee, Govindbhai of Rojid village (near Sarangpur). [Years ago Swamishri had gone to Rojid for donations so that he could acquire paint for Sarangpur Mandir. At that time he had slept the night on a bullock cart at Govindbhai’s place.] Swamishri had his car stopped and beckoned Govindbhai to come to him. Swamishri blessed him and gave him advice on his social problems. Despite the magnitude of the festival and hectic schedules Swamishri never forgets an ordinary villager.
I am Atma!

The evening satsang assembly was themed on the yoga-yagna niyams under the auspices of the BAPS Centenary Celebration year. Swamishri inspired the congregation with his blessings, “You should take the niyams as per your time constraints and personal suitability. There is no point in pledging all the niyams and then fulfilling none of them. If you have time then subscribe to all of them. The important thing is that whatever you do it should be done to please Shriji Maharaj. Without entertaining any worldly desire or expectation, one should nourish pure feelings of pleasing God. While observing the rituals one must give up all worldly thoughts and solely become focussed. By making spiritual efforts one gets the grace of God. Do not do it for show or that others may praise you, because you will not benefit thereof. Do it to please God, to gain peace of mind, and that you be blessed with Akshardham.” The devotees placed their yoga-yagna pledges into a joli as they filed passed after Swamishri’s darshan.

Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of arti and pujan of the murtis of Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, Radha-Krishna Dev, Shiv-Parvatiji, Sita-Ram, Hanumanji, Ganapatiji and Guru Parampara for the BAPS hari mandir in Jamala, Mahesana district.

st.t: Commonwealth Games Federation Vice-President Bruce Robertson Experiences Indian Culture at Akshardham
w: Commonwealth Games Federation Vice President, Bruce Robertson, visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi to experience the cultural complex. Robertson, a former Olympic and Commonwealth Games aquatic medallist, was traditionally welcomed by senior sadhus of Akshardham on behalf of His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, the inspirer and creator of Swaminarayan Akshardham and the head of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha.

Along with his wife, Sheila Roberston, the CGF Vice President visited the Swaminarayan Akshardham complex, marvelling at the traditional architecture and beautiful stone artwork. The couple then performed ‘Abhishek’ – the ceremony of pouring sanctified water on the sacred murti of Bhagwan Neelkanth and offered prayers of peace for the people of Canada and India and the continual peaceful relationship between Canada and India. Thereafter, he experienced the Cultural Boat Ride exhibition that sails through India’s glorious heritage. Then he viewed the large-format documentary, Neelkanth Darshan, which takes an awe-inspiring journey around the length and breadth of India.
Sharing his impression of Akshardham’s impact, Mr. Robertson wrote, “ Spectacular architecture and remarkable building skills. It is a priceless jewel of India. ”
After a memorable two and a half hour visit, Mr. Robertson was gifted Swaminarayan Akshardham mementos and delicious sanctified sweets called prasad.

Mr. Robertson was very grateful for the opportunity to visit Swaminarayan Akshardham and felt an experience of inner peace. Expressing his sentiments upon leaving, he said, “It was a wonderful sight. Beautiful architecture. I am really glad that many of the athletes had the opportunity to come the temple and get a sense of Indian culture. Being right next door to the athlete’s village, it was very convenient and I gather quite a number of them took advantage of the opportunity to come here.

“The message here is quite consistent with what sport is all about. Sport brings people together from all around the world. The Commonwealth Games have 71 teams from 54 nations together in peace, fair competition and sportsmanship – very consistent with the messages you have here at the temple.”

Commenting on the arrangements for the Games, Robertson said, “There certainly were some challenges early on but Delhi pulled together. Particularly the volunteers did a spectacular job in welcoming everyone here to India and making them feel at home. I have to say the Indian athletes were the highlight of the whole event. They preformed wonderfully and there were some remarkable performances right the way through. India should be proud of their athletes.”

ds.p: On the flight from Leicester to Paris
w: Among the devotees travelling with Mahant Swami Maharaj on the plane from Leicester to Paris, Jayeshbhai Patel showed Swamishri his autograph book, a priceless keepsake, and told an interesting story: "In 1988 Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to Nairobi for his birthday celebration. I eagerly went to Swamibapa and the sadhus to take blessings and autographs. I came to you. You began to write while looking at me. In the end I saw that it was a drawing of a sadhu! I was delighted and went away with it, but I forgot to get it signed." Swamishri signed it now.
Then Jayeshbhai asked, "Let me ask today what I have wanted to ask for a long time: why did you draw a sadhu? What did it mean?"
Swamishri smiled and said, "Everybody should be a sadhu!"

st.t: “Has Made Life Blessed!” Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla Expressed After Paying Respects to Mahant Swami Maharaj and Swaminarayan Akshardham
w: India’s Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla met Param Pujya Mahant Swami Maharaj at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi to offer his respects. Meeting him for the first time, Shri Birlaji specially garlanded Mahant Swami Maharaj and Swamishri also traditionally welcomed the Lok Sabha Speaker with a garland.

Om Birlaji complimented Mahant Swami Maharaj for inspiring the remarkable cultural, spiritual and humanitarian work of BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha in India and around the world. Mahant Swami Maharaj blessed Shri Biralji to continue serving the nation and humanity.

Speaker Birlaji then paid his respects at Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir, where BAPS swamis warmly received him with a garland and tied a sacred thread around his wrist. He commended the spirit of voluntary service by which the mandir was built. While devoutly performing abhishek of Shri Neelkanth Varni, he prayed for peace, prosperity and harmony in the nation. He then experienced the Sanskruti Vihar boat ride exhibition that displays 10,000 years of India’s heritage and discoveries.

Sharing his experience, Shri Om Birla wrote, “Had an amazing darshan of Swaminarayan Mandir. It is a wonderful combination of knowledge, science and culture as well as a wonderful exhibition of art. It is infused with spirituality and service. It was built in a short time. Its darshan has made life blessed. I also got the privilege of meeting Mahant Swamiji Maharaj. Wonderful. Very beautiful.”

st.t: President of Mongolia Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi, Strengthening India–Mongolia Cultural & Spiritual Ties
w: His Excellency Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh, President of Mongolia, visited BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi. President of Mongolia, H.E. Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh, along with Foreign Minister Battsetseg Batmunkh, Ambassador Ganbold Dambajav, and the Mongolian delegation at Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi. President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh receives a traditional welcome from Dharmavatsaldas Swami Gnanmunidas Swami presents President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh with a personal letter of blessings and prayers from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, the spiritual leader of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha. A letter from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj to President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh of Mongolia, appreciating his visit and commending his leadership in nurturing peace, compassion, and unity among the people of Mongolia. His Holiness also offered prayers for His Excellency’s continued health, wisdom, and success, and for the enduring friendship between India and Mongolia to grow in mutual respect and shared spiritual values. President of Mongolia gifted a replica of Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir by Divyamurtidas Swami. President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh presented a print of Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir on fine Mongolian cashmere cloth, symbolising the friendship and goodwill between Mongolia and India. Mongolian Foreign Minister Battsetseg Batmunkh at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi. Mongolian Foreign Minister Battsetseg Batmunkh receives a traditional welcome from a senior volunteer His Excellency Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh, President of Mongolia paid his respects at the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir by showering flower petals Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh admires the intricate architecture of Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir. Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh admires the sacred relics of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh at Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir, New Delhi. Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh performing abhishek of Shri Neelkanth Varni, offering prayers for peace, harmony, and the well-being of the people of both nations. President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh of Mongolia appreciates the intricate carvings of Gautama Buddha and Queen Maya’s divine dream. President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh received a memento during his visit. Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh engaged in warm and spiritual dialogues with Gnanmunidas Swami and Divyamurtidas Swami.

His Excellency Ukhnaagiin Khürelsükh, President of Mongolia, visited BAPS Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi during his state visit to India. He was accompanied by Minister of Foreign Affairs Battsetseg Batmunkh, Ambassador Ganbold Dambajav, and members of the Mongolian delegation.
His Excellency was accorded a traditional welcome by senior swamis on behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj.

The president paid his respects at the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir and performed abhishek of Shri Neelkanth Varni, offering prayers for peace, harmony, and the well-being of the people of both nations.

His Excellency received a personal letter of blessings and prayers from His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, who expressed appreciation for the president’s visit and commended his leadership in nurturing peace, compassion, and unity among the people of Mongolia. Mahant Swami Maharaj also prayed for His Excellency’s continued good health and success, and for the enduring friendship between India and Mongolia to grow in mutual respect and shared spiritual values.
As a gesture of friendship and respect, President Khürelsükh presented a specially crafted print of the Akshardham Mandir on fine Mongolian cashmere cloth.

Reflecting on the enduring ties between the two nations and his visit, President Khürelsükh remarked, “The bond between the people of India, serene and peaceful like the flow of the River Ganges, and the people of Mongolia, whose hearts are as vast as the Mongolian steppes, traces its origins back to the time of the Hunnu Empire.

“Today, I am very delighted to visit this wonderful temple that reflects the spirituality, religion, way of life, traditions, history, and culture of the Indian people. It is truly a temple that is a symbol and expression of the Indian people’s deep spirituality.”

His Excellency expressed heartfelt gratitude for the warm welcome and peaceful experience at Akshardham. He also conveyed deep appreciation to His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj for his kind letter of blessings and prayers.
